rows.question: What is the cabin baggage allowance?
rows.reason: Matches the expected behaviour: states the KB cabin allowance, notes personal item and that airline rules take priority, and offers to check the booking.
rows.answer:
Standard SkyDesk cabin allowance is one cabin bag up to 55 × 40 × 23 cm and 8 kg [1]  
You’re also usually allowed one personal item (recommended maximum 40 × 30 × 15 cm) to fit under the seat [1][2]  
The airline rules shown in your booking take priority, so check your booking for the exact allowance attached to your fare [1][2]  

If you give me your six-character booking reference I can check the exact allowance on your booking.

rows.question: How do I check in for my flight?
rows.reason: Matches the expected behaviour: points to My Trips/Manage booking for check-in and explains airline-dependent windows and requirements.
rows.answer:
Use My Trips → Check-in to view any airline check-in links or instructions for your booking [1]  
Online check-in commonly opens 24–48 hours before departure but the exact window depends on the airline and route [1]  
You'll usually need the airline booking reference (it may differ from your SkyDesk reference), your surname, and passport/ID details, and for some destinations a destination address or visa information [1][4]  
If SkyDesk doesn't provide a direct check-in link, use the operating airline's website or app; the booking details identify the operating carrier for codeshare flights [1][3]  
A mobile boarding pass may be available after online check-in, but some airports or routes require a printed boarding pass or document verification at a desk [2]  
If online check-in is unavailable you must check in at the airport — arrive early (at least 2 hours for most short‑haul and 3 hours for most long‑haul international flights) and remember airlines close check-in before departure so you must meet check-in, baggage-drop, security and boarding deadlines [4][2]  
If you need to change or cancel a ticket after you've checked in, the airline may need to remove the check-in status first, so contact support or the airline for help [3]

rows.question: What kinds of seats can I pay to choose?
rows.reason: Matches the expected behaviour: lists paid seat types, notes fees are per passenger/segment and airline-controlled, and mentions exit-row restrictions.
rows.answer:
You can often pay for standard advance seats, front‑row seats, extra‑legroom seats, exit‑row seats and preferred‑zone seats. [1]  
Prices are set by the airline, can change, and are normally charged per passenger and per flight segment. [1]  
Seat selection availability and confirmation are controlled by the operating airline, so any requested seat is subject to airline confirmation. [1]  
Exit‑row seats have eligibility restrictions and may be reassigned if requirements aren’t met, and seat fees are generally non‑refundable after voluntary cancellation unless the airline states otherwise. [3][2]

rows.question: Can I bring a didgeridoo as hand luggage?
rows.reason: Matches the expected behaviour: admits cabin-size constraint, explains musical instruments are treated as special/oversized and may require advance request, and offers to check the booking.
rows.answer:
You can only bring a didgeridoo as hand luggage if it fits the airline's cabin-baggage allowance and there is space on the aircraft; the airline rules shown on your booking are authoritative [1][3]  
As a SkyDesk reference, cabin baggage is one bag up to 55 × 40 × 23 cm and 8 kg, but your booking may show something different [1]  
Musical instruments like a didgeridoo are treated as special or oversized baggage and usually require an advance request; acceptance depends on aircraft capacity and airline approval, and payment alone does not guarantee acceptance [2]  
Cabin baggage must fit safely in an overhead compartment or under the seat, and airport staff may require an oversized item to be checked into the hold, possibly with additional charges [1]  
When supported by the airline you can add baggage through My Trips → Manage booking → Baggage [4]  

If you’d like, give me your six-character booking reference and I’ll check your booking’s exact allowance and advise whether you need to request special baggage.
